**Title (English, from literature):** Disparaging the training rules

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Vilekhana* ("Disparaging the training rules") is the seventy-second rule in the *Pācittiya* chapter of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. The rule provides that a monk who speaks disparagingly of or criticizes the monastic code (*sikkhāpada*) commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [Blackstone 1995]. In secondary literature on the monastic discipline, Kathryn R. Blackstone (drawing on Jotiya Dhirasekera) notes that Pācittiya 72 explicitly prohibits monks from disparaging training rules, a statute that bears directly on historical monastic debates regarding the definition and attempted rescission of the "lesser and minor" rules [Blackstone 1995]. The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
